title: Eccentric Exercise in Community-dwelling Older Adults
official: The Effects of an Eccentric-biased Strengthening Programme Delivered to Community-dwelling Older Adults"
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effectiveness of a 12-month eccentric-biased strengthening programme in community-dwelling older adults aged 65 years and older. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can an eccentric-biased strengthening programme be feasibly delivered to community-dwelling older adults in a community setting? Does participation in the programme improve functional mobility, lower-limb strength, falls self-efficacy, and health-related quality of life?

Participants will:

Attend a 12-month supervised eccentric-biased strengthening programme delivered in a community setting.

Complete assessments of functional mobility, lower-limb strength, falls self-efficacy, and health-related quality of life before and after the intervention.

Provide information regarding their experience of participating in the programme to evaluate its acceptability.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Age ≥ 65 years Ambulant with or without a walking aid

Exclusion Criteria:

* Inability to provide informed consent, assessed using the Mental Capacity Act two-stage assessment
